config.name: Astro Buyer Copy Guidelines
config.source: UX Writing Playbook (1).zip, files listed in domains.buyer.sourceDocuments
config.note: Domain supplement, not an independently approved company policy. Not active in existing Figma/Chrome tools. Apply shared Global Principles separately.

sharedGlobalFoundation.note: Reference the existing global baseline; buyer-only guidelines are below. Do not copy or enforce Supplier-specific guidelines or glossary.

buyer.label: Buyer
buyer.audience: Buyers using Astro consumer products. Check actual product, journey stage, and audience before applying copy rules.

reviewPolicy.drafts: All Buyer rules are extracted from the uploaded UX Writing Playbook and are OFF until reviewed for current use.
reviewPolicy.nonFabrication: Do not invent benefits, promo terms, delivery promises, urgency, eligibility, stock claims, or payment consequences.
reviewPolicy.scope: Buyer product UX. Do not automatically apply Buyer capitalization, voice, or marketing tone to Supplier, Mitra, or Admin.

toneReference.source: 2.4. Our Tone.pdf; 2.5. Our Tone_ User Journey Map.pdf; 2.6. Writing with Voice & Tone.pdf
toneReference.buyerBaseline: More casual, fun, enthusiastic and simple than operational product tones; adjust to specific situation.
toneReference.journeyNuance: First impressions, onboarding, promo news and payment success may lean more exciting; payment details, confirmation and errors should lean toward respectful reassurance.
toneReference.caution: Tone is context-dependent; payment and errors should never sacrifice clarity or sensitivity for playfulness.

guidelines.name: Use a friendly, thoughtful and reliable voice.
guidelines.rule: Use natural, relatable language while staying helpful, considerate, and clear. Avoid jokes or overly casual expressions in sensitive or confusing moments.

guidelines.name: Match tone to the user's journey.
guidelines.rule: Use an engaging tone where appropriate, while prioritizing respect and reassurance during payment-related uncertainty and errors.

guidelines.name: Lead with what matters to the buyer.
guidelines.rule: Prioritize what users need to understand and the benefit relevant to them, rather than internal company objectives. Do not invent benefits.

guidelines.name: Make content easy to scan.
guidelines.rule: Use descriptive headings, logical information grouping, and short paragraphs; use bullet points only when they help.

guidelines.name: Keep copy plain and concise.
guidelines.rule: Use familiar words, active voice, and short natural sentences. Remove unnecessary words without losing material information.

guidelines.name: Use familiar acronyms carefully.
guidelines.rule: Avoid unexplained industry jargon; spell out unfamiliar acronyms on first use when helpful. Keep widely recognized acronyms or official entity names as needed.

guidelines.name: Apply Buyer capitalization appropriately.
guidelines.rule: Playbook guidance: sentence case for headings/body and title case for buttons and section labels; preserve proper names. Validate against current Buyer Design System before enforcing.

guidelines.name: Keep brand naming consistent.
guidelines.rule: Use 'Astro' in product UX writing; the stylized ASTRO logo is a separate brand asset.

guidelines.name: Use consistent number, currency, date and time formats.
guidelines.rule: Playbook examples include numerals, %, 'Rp50.000', 24-hour times with WIB when relevant, date names in Indonesian/English context, and no-space en dashes for ranges. Do not change actual values.

guidelines.name: Use emphasis and punctuation purposefully.
guidelines.rule: Avoid overly emphatic punctuation, excessive emoji, all caps, and gratuitous bold. Emphasize the most helpful information.

glossary.preferredUsage: Use 'Astro' in UX copy; logo styling may differ.
Preserve proper product naming when relevant; verify current naming.
